'''FrontierMath''' is a [[test bed]] to [[benchmark (computing)|benchmark]]<ref>{{cite arXiv |last1=Glazer |first1=Elliot |title=FrontierMath: A Benchmark for Evaluating Advanced Mathematical Reasoning in AI |date=2025-12-23 |eprint=2411.04872 |last2=Erdil |first2=Ege |last3=Besiroglu |first3=Tamay |last4=Chicharro |first4=Diego |last5=Chen |first5=Evan |last6=Gunning |first6=Alex |last7=Olsson |first7=Caroline Falkman |last8=Denain |first8=Jean-Stanislas |last9=Ho |first9=Anson |class=cs.AI }}</ref> various [[artificial intelligence]] systems in their attempts to solve 14 bespoke<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mindstudio.ai/blog/frontier-math-benchmark-open-research-problems-ai-reasoning/|title=What Is the Frontier Math Benchmark? Why Open Research Problems Expose True AI Reasoning|first=MindStudio|last=Team|date=April 7, 2026|website=MindStudio}}</ref> heretofore unexamined mathematical problems<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://epoch.ai/frontiermath/open-problems|title=FrontierMath: Open Problems - Unsolved Mathematical Challenges|website=Epoch AI}}</ref> (none of which are on the scale of the [[Millennium Problems]]).  It was established by the [[nonprofit organization|non-profit]] research organization Epoch AI in November 2024.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://spectrum.ieee.org/ai-math-benchmarks|title=AI Math Benchmarks: AI's Growing Capabilities - IEEE Spectrum|website=spectrum.ieee.org}}</ref> The first such open problem{{Mdash}}of the "moderately interesting" rank{{Mdash}}to be solved was in [[hypergraph]] theory: "A Constant-Factor Lower Bound For ''H'' (''n)''"  by [[GPT-5.4]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.remio.ai/post/gpt-5-4-solves-its-first-open-math-problem-from-frontiermath-benchmark|title=GPT-5.4 solves its first open math problem from FrontierMath benchmark|first=Olivia|last=Johnson|date=March 14, 2026|website=remio}}</ref>
